chunks: Ahmad, from Al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about an ostrich egg which I ate in the Al-Haram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give in charity with its price'.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for eating an ostrich egg in the Haram?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific expiation (*kaffarah*) for consuming ostrich eggs within the sacred precincts (*Al-Haram*). It demonstrates the Shia juristic principle of applying monetary compensation based on the item's value when the primary prohibition involves consuming game, thereby linking ritual sanctity with tangible financial restitution.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Sa’d Bin Abdullah who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about an ostrich egg which I ate in the Al-Harram. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give in charity with its price’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ahmad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Sa‘d ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of my eating ostrich eggs in al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ‘You must give its price in charity.’”
